Name: King Slime
Summoning:
Manual:
King Slime can be summoned by using the Slime Crown, in any biome at any time.
Random:
King Slime has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance of naturally spawning while the following conditions are met:
- The potential spawn point is located in one of the outer lateral sixths of the map (the far left or far right).
- The depth at its potential spawn point is above zero.
- It is daytime.
- King Slime is not currently alive in the world.
- The player is not in a Graveyard biome.
- There is no water or less than 1 tile of water above its potential spawn point.
- There must be standard, green grass at its potential spawn point (off-screen; see NPC spawning)
  - If the spawn succeeds, King Slime will spawn in a random place around the player and not necessarily on this grass block.
Slime Rain:
If 150 slimes are killed by players, NPCs, traps, lava, and/or summoned minions during the Slime Rain event, King Slime spawns. The following slimes will count toward this total as long as they are killed during the event: Baby Slime, Black Slime, Blue Slime, Green Slime, Jungle Slime, Pinky, Purple Slime, Red Slime, and Yellow Slime. Statue-spawned slimes are eligible as well. Defeating King Slime ends the event shortly after. If all players die, King Slime despawns, and the event continues for some time before ending on its own (between 9 and 15 in-game hours). If King Slime has already been defeated in a world, it only takes 75 slime kills to spawn him. If King Slime is summoned manually with the Slime Crown and then subsequently killed, while the Slime Rain is active, the event ends in the same way as if the player killed the King Slime that naturally spawns at the end of the event. This can be quite helpful for players in later stages of the game who want to get the Slime Rain event over with as quickly as possible.
Remix:
In Remix worlds, killing a slime has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of spawning King Slime, provided the boss has not yet been defeated, is not already alive, and at least one player has more than 140 maximum health and more than 8 defense. Only the death of certain types of slime can trigger this: Baby Slime, Black Slime, Blue Slime, Green Slime, Jungle Slime, Pinky, Purple Slime, Red Slime, and Yellow Slime. Statue-spawned slimes are eligible as well. Slimes killed without the player dealing damage to them will not spawn King Slime.
Aftermath:
- Defeating King Slime for the first time spawns Nerdy Slime.
- The Angler will be able to ask for Angelfish and Cloudfish if he could not already.
- If Queen Slime has already been defeated, the Princess will begin selling Royal Romance.
- The Demolitionist will begin to sell Freeze Bombs during Night if he was not already.
- The Traveling Merchant will be able to sell the Gray Zapinator if he could not already.
Tips:
- Piercing weapons can not only damage King Slime, but also kill the additional slimes he spawns.
- When King Slime is about to teleport, he shrinks and his map icon will get closer towards the ground. The latter can be used to know when he is about to return if he goes offscreen.
- The Blue Slimes that are spawned during the fight can drop Hearts and Stars, which respectively restore 20 health and 100 mana.
- Due to the high number of Blue Slimes spawned during the fight, summoning King Slime while in specific areas can be a quick, easy way to farm for specific drops. Examples include Biome Keys, Pirate Maps, Halloween and Christmas drops, or the Cascade, Hel-Fire, Amarok, Yelets, and Kraken yoyos.
  - While Blue Slimes cannot drop Souls of Light or Souls of Night, they can be converted to Shimmer Slimes which can.
- King Slime himself does not drop any Gel, but the Blue Slimes he spawns do. This makes fighting him a good way to farm Gel, e.g. for Flamethrower ammo or Asphalt Blocks.
- Killing King Slime on Expert Mode and selling all drops gives 10 Gold on average.
- When King Slime teleports, he can become stuck inside the blocks around him, preventing his movement for a while.

Name: Eye of Cthulhu
Summoning:
Manual:
The Eye of Cthulhu can be summoned manually using a Suspicious Looking Eye at night (from 7:30 PM to 4:30 AM). Only one Eye of Cthulhu can be summoned manually at a time.
Random:
The Eye of Cthulhu can also spawn naturally at the start of the night. Its arrival when spawning naturally is announced by the status message “You feel an evil presence watching you...”.
In order for the boss to spawn naturally, the following conditions must be fulfilled at dusk (7:30 PM):
- The Eye of Cthulhu has not yet been defeated in the current world or no placed Demon/Crimson Altars exist in the current world.
- At least one player in the world has at least 200 maximum health and at least 11 defense.
- At least four town NPCs are present in the world. While the Old Man, Traveling Merchant, and town pets count towards this total, the Skeleton Merchant does not.
- No boss is already alive.
- None of the following events are active: Lantern Night, Old One's Army, Pumpkin Moon, or Frost Moon.
- Time is not being accelerated by the Enchanted Sundial or Enchanted Moondial.
If the conditions are met, there is a 1/3 (33.33%) chance for the Eye of Cthulhu to spawn.[a] Provided the roll succeeds, the status message appears and a hidden countdown of 1 minute 21 seconds begins. The Eye of Cthulhu spawns at the end of the countdown, at 8:51 PM. Another check is performed at that time, with all of the following conditions needing to be fulfilled in order for the boss to spawn:
- At least one player is in the surface or Space layer.
  - Consequently, the natural spawning of the Eye of Cthulhu can easily be prevented by remaining in a layer lower than the surface for the night. Returning to the surface before dawn will cause it to spawn as normal.
  - This restriction is lifted in worlds where the world spawn point is below the surface, such as worlds with the special world seed Remix active or the secret world seed Mole people. The Eye of Cthulhu can spawn naturally in those worlds regardless of the player's position, whether they are above or below the surface.
- No boss is already alive.
- The Lunar Events are not active and the countdown for the spawning of the Moon Lord has not begun, either due to manual summoning or defeating the fourth Celestial Pillar.
- Time is not being accelerated by the Enchanted Sundial or Enchanted Moondial.
In singleplayer, exiting the world during the countdown also prevents the Eye of Cthulhu from spawning naturally.
In worlds where the special seeds For the Worthy and The Constant are present but Celebration Mk 10 is not, The Eye of Cthulhu will still be able to randomly spawn, even if it has been defeated before.
ExpertMode:
In Expert Mode, the Eye of Cthulhu has the following extra properties:
- The Eye of Cthulhu spawns more Servants of Cthulhu than normal, as well as 4–5 extra Servants of Cthulhu upon transforming.
- In the second phase, the Eye of Cthulhu will gain an additional powerful rapid chain dash attack, during which it lets out a higher-pitched roar every time it dashes. At first, the Eye of Cthulhu's chain dashes are performed after its regular ones but they will eventually replace the standard dashes and become faster and trigger more often as the Eye of Cthulhu's life decreases, dashing nearly continuously when close to death.
- The Eye of Cthulhu will have negative defense when it reaches very low health (which increases damage dealt to it):
  - −15 defense when below 12% health (436 / 556), which means it takes 7 more damage per hit (15 more damage from critical hits).
  - −30 defense when below 4% health (145 / 185), which means it takes 15 more damage per hit (30 more damage from critical hits).
Aftermath:
- The Angler will be able to ask for Angelfish and Cloudfish if he could not already.
- The Dryad will be able to move in if she could not already.
- The Traveling Merchant will begin selling Code 1, and will begin selling the Gray Zapinator if he was not already.
Tips:
- The Eye of Cthulhu drops either Demonite or Crimtane Ore. While the corresponding set of armor and a number of tools additionally require Shadow Scales or Tissue Samples respectively—which the Eye does not drop—the sword, bow, axe, yoyo, whip, and fishing pole can be crafted with only the bars.
- Due to the ease of crafting its summoning item and relatively low difficulty, farming the Eye of Cthulhu is one of the more effective ways of making money prior to Hardmode. It drops 3 Gold / 7 Gold 50 Silver up front, plus ores which can be sold as bars for twice (Demonite) or triple (Crimtane) that amount.
- The Eye of Cthulhu will only spawn randomly if a player has more than 10 defense. Taking defense-boosting equipment off before dusk can prevent it from spawning randomly.
- The boss looks at the player it will follow, which can be helpful information in multiplayer.
- It is most vulnerable during its transformation, because it neither moves nor attacks. However, there is only a brief window of opportunity for this.
- Because there are no location-based requirements for summoning, defeating multiple Eyes of Cthulhu in an area can be an effective setup for harder boss fights as the dropped Hearts can be picked up mid-fight as needed, though killing an Eye of Cthulhu for that purpose must be balanced with the time it takes away from killing a night-only boss.
- Since Crimtane Ore and Bars sell for a 30% higher price than their Demonite counterparts, farming the Eye of Cthulhu in a Crimson world is more profitable.
- In singleplayer, the player can repeatedly pause the game using Autopause in order to properly aim at the Eye of Cthulhu during its dash attacks.

Name: Eater of Worlds
Summoning:
The Eater of Worlds spawns upon destroying every third Shadow Orb in a Corruption world.
It can also be summoned manually by using a Worm Food in The Corruption or Underground Corruption, at any time.
ExpertMode:
- In Expert Mode, the Eater of Worlds has 5 extra body segments, all of its segments are 20% larger in size, and have 2 extra defense. It also has 20% increased maximum speed, and accelerates over twice as fast.
  - The increased speed allows it to reach a maximum height of approximately 44 tiles when burrowing out of tiles at full speed, before falling down.
- The Eater of Worlds will randomly shoot Vile Spit from its head and body segments, as long as the segments have an unobstructed line of sight to the player. The Vile Spit projectiles can be destroyed in a single hit from any attack or projectile.
  - Body segments have a 1/900 (0.11%) chance per tick (average of once every 15 seconds) to shoot Vile Spit. They also can only shoot when they are above surface and are not in front of any background walls.
  - Head segments shoot more often as their individual health decreases. The chance for them to shoot Vile Spit gradually increases from 1/390 (0.26%) per tick (average of once every 6.5 seconds) at full health to 1/90 (1.11%) per tick (average of once every 1.5 seconds) just before dying.
- The Eater of Worlds takes 80% less damage from the following projectiles and explosives (this damage reduction is applied before defense):
Aftermath:
- The Tavernkeep will begin to spawn as the Unconscious Man.
- The meteorites will now be able to land.
- The Dryad will be able to move in if she could not already.
- The Merchant will begin selling the Drum Set and Drumstick if he was not already.
- The Arms Dealer will begin selling Unholy Arrows at night if he was not already.
- The Angler will be able to ask for Angelfish and Cloudfish if he could not already.
- The Traveling Merchant will be able to sell the Gray Zapinator if he could not already.
Tips:
- If the player manages to quickly find the initial spawning location of Eater of Worlds, they can attack it with a piercing weapon while it is still in its coiled state, which will damage many of its segments at once and can potentially kill it in seconds.
- Effective weapons include piercing or area-of-effect weapons, such as the Vilethorn, Spiky Balls, whips, and fast melee weapons, such as the Falcon Blade and the Terragrim.
  - In Classic Mode, Grenades are an effective weapon against the Eater. That is not true in higher difficulties, since the Eater gains resistance to explosives.
- Like other worm-types, once the Eater's head passes a given point, every body segment must follow. This allows the player to stand next to the body, attacking every segment as it goes by. The player should be wary of the head looping back around.
- Killing the head of the Eater of Worlds causes its speed to drastically decrease, almost to a stop.
- If possible, try to aim for the head or tail of each section, as if they die first, the Eater of Worlds will not split. Note that the head is far more vulnerable.
- If fighting in a chasm, be wary of getting surrounded, which can lead to death very quickly, especially in Expert or Master Mode. A quick way to escape is to have a Bed to teleport to (using Recall Potions or a Magic or Ice Mirror) above the battle area.
  - It may be preferable to hollow out an area in the Corruption in advance, in order to avoid this situation.
- Farming the Eater of Worlds is particularly profitable, being one of the most effective ways of making money prior to Hardmode.
  - Converting the Demonite Ore to bars and selling its drops will yield an average of 19 Gold per kill.
  - If Vile Mushrooms run short, Vile Powder (for Worm Food) can be bought from the Dryad during a Blood Moon.
- Since each segment can drop loot when killed, it can be a good source of Presents during Christmas, and Goodie Bags, Bloody Machetes, and Bladed Gloves during Halloween.
- In Hardmode, it can provide other items as well:
  - It is a good way to farm for a Corruption Key, as every segment has a chance of dropping one.
  - In a Corrupt Snow biome, it can drop Amaroks, with each selling for a base value of 4 Gold.
  - In a Corrupt Ocean, it can drop Pirate Maps.
- The Eater of Worlds will start to flee underground if the player leaves the Corruption biome, but will not immediately despawn. Players can utilize this mechanic to keep the Eater of Worlds away from themselves without despawning it by moving in and out of the Corruption, watching for the boss's icon on the minimap to make sure it does not leave.
- Using a flail will block any Vile Spit from hitting the player when ⚒ Use / Attack is held down. Alternatively, a whip would also work for it can sweep a large area clean of Vile Spit in a single whip.

Name: Brain of Cthulhu
Summoning:
The Brain of Cthulhu spawns upon destroying every third Crimson Heart in a Crimson world.
It can also be summoned manually by using a Bloody Spine in The Crimson or Underground Crimson, at any time.
ExpertMode:
In Expert Mode, the second phase has three mirror images of the Brain appear around the player, mirroring the Brain's movements and becoming more opaque as the boss loses health. The Creepers also behave much more aggressively and gain increased movement speed.
Furthermore, both the Creepers (in the first phase) and the Brain (in the second phase) inflict a random debuff upon contact. The probabilities of applying each debuff are listed in the following table; note that the Creepers always inflict a debuff while the Brain only has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to do so.
Aftermath:
- The Tavernkeep will begin to spawn as the Unconscious Man.
- Meteorites will now be able to land.
- The Dryad will be able to move in if she could not already.
- The Merchant will begin selling the Drum Set and Drumstick if he was not already.
- The Arms Dealer will begin selling Unholy Arrows at night if he was not already.
- The Angler will be able to ask for Angelfish and Cloudfish if he could not already.
- The Traveling Merchant will begin selling the Gray Zapinator if he was not already.
Tips:
- Creepers have low individual health and are especially susceptible to the On Fire! and Frostburn debuffs. Weapons that inflict these debuffs can make quick work of them.
- Grenades and other splash damage weapons can kill the Creepers very quickly, as they will bunch up often.
- Since the Brain of Cthulhu is susceptible to knockback, weapons with high knockback such as The Rotted Fork can keep both Creepers and the Brain from closing distance between teleports. It is also possible to use early-game melee weapons such as the Katana or the Zombie Arm as long as they do not have disadvantageous modifiers. It is preferable to use spears for this fight since they deal more knockback, however, so the Trident or The Rotted Fork is recommended.
  - Note that this may not work in Expert Mode and Master Mode, since it might be hard to tell which Brain to attack among the illusions.
- Jester's Arrows or other piercing weapons can be immensely helpful while fighting the first stage, since Creepers often group up in a clustered formation, effectively allowing the player to hit most if not all of the Creepers in one well-aimed shot.
- The Minishark is extremely effective in keeping the Brain of Cthulhu away from the player during the second stage.
- There are several methods to reveal the real Brain of Cthulhu in the second stage:
  - The real Brain is the only one with a health bar.
  - Bone Javelins only stick out of the real Brain.
  - Minions and sentries will target the real Brain.
  - The On Fire!, Frostburn, and Poisoned debuffs only damage the real Brain, as well as apply visual effects.
  - The Slime Gun and Water Gun only apply visual effects onto the real Brain, though they cannot inflict damage.
  - The Slime Mount only bounces off the real Brain.
  - The illusions position themselves in relation to the player. The illusions will quickly spread away from the real Brain if the player is walking away from it, but the real Brain will continue to move at a steady pace.
  - When using a controller, the lock on feature will only target the real Brain.
- Selling all the Crimtane Ore that can be obtained from the fight is a very effective method to make money in pre-Hardmode.

Name: Queen Bee
Summoning:
The Queen Bee spawns upon breaking a Larva found inside Bee Hives in the Underground Jungle.
She can also be summoned manually by using an Abeemination in the Jungle or Underground Jungle, at any time.
Aftermath:
- The Witch Doctor will be able to move in.
- The Angler will be able to ask for Angelfish and Cloudfish if he could not already.
- The Traveling Merchant will begin selling the Gray Zapinator if he was not already.
Tips:
- The Honey naturally found in Bee Hives can be used to craft Bottled Honey, provide passive health regeneration mid-fight, and help to negate the potency of being afflicted by Poisoned. However, standing in Honey will slow down the player significantly, so prolonged submersion is not recommended.
- Equipping a Bezoar can help the player avoid taking large amounts of damage from being afflicted with Poisoned, especially in Expert and Master Mode due to its significantly extended duration, where it can reach upwards of 25 seconds.
- The Bees do little damage, but can easily become an annoyance as they can push the player around. If the player does not have a Cobalt Shield or Obsidian Shield to avoid knockback, any grappling hook can be used to anchor the player to blocks.
  - In Classic difficulty, a spinning flail is sufficient to kill any incoming Bees before they can reach the player.
  - Bees will target other enemies if they are closer than the player and can thus be distracted with statue-spawned enemies or other trapped enemies.
  - In Expert and Master Mode, Bees are much tougher and can easily kill the player if ignored.
  - The Lightning Aura sentry summons and the Explosive Trap sentry summons can easily kill the bees if the player is near them.
- The Queen Bee can be a viable source of money, dropping 5 Gold upon death and additional profit from her drops, as well as being comparably simple to summon.
- The Obsidian armor is a great choice for summoners looking to focus on whips.
- If the Shield of Cthulhu's dash is timed well, the damage of the Queen Bee's charging attacks can be blocked. However, this strategy will become less reliable over time due to the Queen Bee's speed ramping up significantly as her health is lowered.
- For ranged players, any bow in combination with piercing arrows (such as Unholy or Jester's Arrows) can be a good choice for quickly dispatching the summoned Bees.

Name: Skeletron
Summoning:
Summoning Skeletron requires the player to speak to the Old Man at the Dungeon's entrance at night. Upon selecting the "Curse" option, he will turn into Skeletron. Skeletron can only be summoned once per night, as the Old Man will not respawn until dawn.
Once Skeletron is defeated, the Old Man's curse will be lifted and he will no longer appear. Skeletron will thereafter only be summonable with the Clothier Voodoo Doll. Killing the Clothier at night with this accessory equipped will summon Skeletron.
A special variant of Skeletron can be summoned via Chippy's Couch. See Red Hat variant below.
ExpertMode:
Skeletron has additional properties in Expert Mode:
- The defense of its head is increased by 25 for each of its hands, resulting in a total defense of 60, initially. Once one hand is defeated, it drops to 35 and finally to 10 when both hands are defeated.
  - During the spinning attack, Skeletron's defense is therefore also only reduced to 50 / 25. Only when both hands are defeated, it will be reduced to 0 like in Classic Mode.
- While spinning, the head gets a 30% damage boost, making it deal 91 / 137 damage.
- Skeletron will inflict debuffs upon contact with the player: its hands are able to inflict Slow for 1–2 / 1.5–2.5 seconds, and the head is able to inflict Bleeding for 6–10 / 7.5–12.5 seconds.
- Hand slashes are 50% more frequent and receive a 16% speed increase.
  - Additionally, the hands return to the head faster after their attack.Verify
- The head accelerates and moves faster when not spinning.
- The spin attack has its speed increased by 233%. Additionally, it gets further increases under certain circumstances:
  - 5% increased when one hand is defeated, and 10% when both are defeated.
  - If the player is 9.375 tiles away or more, its speed gets multiplied by 1.1 for every 3.125 tiles above this threshold, up to 2.6× speed when at 37.5 tiles away.
- Once either of the hands are destroyed or the head's health is reduced to below 75% (6,600 / 8,415), the head begins to shoot homing skulls at the player that despawn on contact with a solid block. It shoots one skull roughly every 1.33 seconds, and doubles the frequency to one skull roughly every 0.67 seconds once both hands are defeated. It pauses firing during its spin attack.
- Skeletron moves faster and has better AI when targeting multiple players. With this, it is able to "stun-lock" the player while spinning, able to almost instantly kill them if they are not able to escape (e.g. by using a hook).
Aftermath:
- Defeating Skeletron for the first time grants unlimited access to all Dungeon areas for players within the current world, furthermore preventing Dungeon Guardians from spawning.
- The Clothier will be able to move in.
- Items that require Bones in their crafting recipes can now be decrafted via Shimmer.
- Enemies in the Underworld gain a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of dropping the Cascade yoyo as long as Hardmode has not been activated.
- Lava Slimes can now rarely be replaced by Hell Slimes.
- The Golfer will begin selling the Golf Cart Keys once the player also has a golf score above 1999.
- The Merchant will begin selling Safes, and will begin selling the Drum Set and Drumstick if he was not already.
- The Arms Dealer will begin selling the Quad-Barrel Shotgun when spoken to in a Graveyard.
- The Dryad will be able to move in if she could not already.
- The Angler will be able to ask for Angelfish and Cloudfish if he could not already.
- The Traveling Merchant will be able to sell the Gray Zapinator if he could not already, and be able to sell the Sitting Duck's Fishing Pole.
- Old Shaking Chests begin to rarely spawn in the Cavern layer. Unlocking the chest with ⚷ Open / Activate while the player has a Golden Key in their inventory releases the Elder Slime.
Tips:
- Defeating Skeletron is not necessary for game progression until Golem has been defeated. The Cultists, required for initiating the Lunar Events, will only spawn once both Golem and Skeletron have been defeated. However, skipping Skeletron in pre-Hardmode results in a lack of valuable Dungeon loot, keeps Shadow Chests from being opened (due to the inaccessible Shadow Key), blocks access to the Mechanic, as well as renders the Safe and Void Vault unobtainable.
- Try to avoid staying above or far to one side of Skeletron for a long time. It will accelerate to move back above the player during this time, and it can be hard to avoid both the head and hands as they rebound into position.
- The Slime Mount can help the player escape Skeletron's head-spin attack.
- Using a grappling hook can also help evade Skeletron's attacks and is an especially useful tool to escape its head-spin attack.
- With multiple players, it is a good idea to set the spawn point near the Dungeon, so that players can simply rejoin the fight if they die.
- Attacking the hands first is advised, as destroying them both will make it very easy to dodge Skeletron for the rest of the battle.
  - This is pretty much mandatory in Expert Mode, as Skeletron gains 25 defense for each hand it has alive.
  - Moving quickly enough on a minecart can cause the hands to despawn.
- In Expert Mode, if the player keeps moving in different directions, most of the homing skulls will miss.
  - The player can also jump in a circle around Skeletron's head, aided by a Shield of Cthulhu or Featherfall Potion.
  - Skulls are blocked by solid blocks, so a barrier between the player and Skeletron can let the player attack Skeletron using a yoyo with impunity.
- Shimmering a Bezoar lets the player use a Adhesive Bandage for the fight, blocking the Bleeding debuff for more value out of health regeneration buffs.

Name: Deerclops
Summoning:
Deerclops can be summoned manually by using a Deer Thing in the Snow or Ice biome, at any time.
Deerclops can also spawn naturally at midnight (12:00 AM) in the surface Snow biome during a Blizzard when the following conditions are fulfilled:
- At least one player in the world is in the surface Snow biome.
  - This player has at least 200 maximum health or at least 9 defense.
  - There are no town NPCs within a 240×135-tile rectangle centered on this player.
- There are no other bosses already alive.
- None of the following events are active: Old One's Army, Pumpkin Moon, Frost Moon, or any invasion.
  - Note that this excludes certain events, such as the Blood Moon. They do not prevent Deerclops from spawning.
- No Martian Probe is alive.
- The countdown for the spawning of the Moon Lord has not begun, either due to manual summoning or defeating the fourth Celestial Pillar.
- In Remix and Zenith worlds, Deerclops will only naturally spawn in Snow biomes on the Surface layer, where the Blizzard visual effect is not displayed.
  - Deerclops will not spawn in the Cavern layer where the Blizzard effect is displayed.
If Deerclops has previously been defeated in the world, there is only a 1/4 (25%) chance for it to spawn naturally at midnight.
Tips:
- There are no prerequisite bosses that are required to be defeated in order to summon this boss. However, Deerclops' strength may warrant waiting until the player has defeated the Eater of Worlds or the Brain of Cthulhu to fight it.
  - With sufficient skill, the Deerclops can be defeated earlier in game progression, which can be helpful to the player during pre-Hardmode.
- A Warmth Potion is useful when fighting Deerclops, as the boss is affected by its buff. In addition, one may find it useful to bring a Hand Warmer to the battle, since the Frozen debuff can easily cause the player to die quickly if inflicted.
- Building a platform of non-solid blocks about 6 tiles (twice the height of the player) up in the air, along with staircases made of solid blocks on either side to allow Deerclops to get on, can elevate it high enough above the ground to prevent the boss from using its debris attack entirely, making the fight much easier.Verify
- Due to being able to inflict Slow from a large range, accessories like the Anklet of the Wind or Magiluminescence alongside Swiftness Potions can help make the fight much more manageable.
- Avoid lingering directly above Deerclops, as the Shadow Hands it summons in this situation are very dangerous.
- The player can run between Deerclops's legs without taking damage. This is useful for avoiding the first two Ice Spike attacks, but the player should not stick around for the third.
- Players should place their spawn point away from where Deerclops can wander, as it can stay around the spawn area.
  - This is especially recommended for Mediumcore players, as they can be left defenseless near Deerclops if they die in the middle of the fight.
- The Frozen debuff from the Ice Spike attack is capable of interrupting a player's extending grappling hook, causing them to drop to the ground. Avoid moving over large gaps to prevent unnecessary damage.

Name: Wall of Flesh
KbResist: 20%/28%/36% (1 player)69% (2 players)79% (3 players)86%  (4 players)100% (5 players or more) (1 player)72% (2 players)82% (3 players)88% (4 players)100% (5 players or more)
Summoning:
The Wall of Flesh can be summoned by dropping a Guide Voodoo Doll into lava in The Underworld while the Guide is alive, which destroys the Guide Voodoo Doll and kills the Guide in the process. Alternatively, the boss can also be summoned by letting the Guide die within lava in The Underworld. He can die by any means (the player, an enemy, or the environment), as long as he is touching lava when he dies.
The Wall of Flesh is summoned just beyond the player's screen on the side where the Guide Voodoo Doll was dropped into lava (or where the Guide was killed by lava), then moves in the direction of the player. As a general rule, it spawns at least 75 tiles away from the player.
Technical details:
When the Guide Voodoo Doll is destroyed or the Guide is killed in lava, the game checks whether all players are horizontally at least 75 tiles away from the location of the doll/Guide. If they are, then the Wall of Flesh is spawned at that horizontal position. Otherwise, the game moves one tile towards the closest lateral world border and checks again, repeating this until it encounters a tile that is horizontally at least 75 tiles away from any player. It stops 20 tiles before the true world border (i.e. 21/22 tiles away from the visible world border), even if a player is still within 75 tiles at that point (e.g. standing directly against the visible world border).
After locating the horizontal spawn position, the game determines a valid vertical position. The spawning tile must not be occupied by a solid block and its liquid level must not exceed 100 (i.e. at most approx. 39% of the tile can contain liquid). Again, the game begins at the vertical position of the doll/Guide and checks if that location is valid. Then it checks one tile above that spot and one tile below it, then two tiles above and two tiles below, and so on, until finding a valid spot. If the game finds no valid spot after 1000 attempts (i.e. 1000 tiles above and below), then it reverts to the initial vertical position. Finally, the vertical limits are enforced: If the vertical position that was encountered is higher than 10 tiles below the Cavern–Underworld border, it is forcibly moved down to that position (even though the tile there was not considered valid before), and if it is lower than 80 tiles below that border (roughly the vertical center of the Underworld), it is forcibly moved up to that position (again, even though the tile at that position was not considered valid before).
The center of the Wall of Flesh's mouth appears at the determined location, and the eyes are spawned relative to it. The boss quickly aligns itself vertically with the player after spawning.
Aftermath:
When the Wall of Flesh is killed, it leaves its drops in a midair 9×9-tile frame of Demonite Bricks (in Corruption worlds) or Crimtane Bricks (in Crimson worlds). It will also always drop the Pwnhammer, which is required to generate Hardmode ores in the world (through breaking Demon or Crimson Altars with a hammer of 80% hammer power or higher, of which the Pwnhammer is the first obtained).
- In Expert Mode or higher difficulties, its dropped Treasure Bag includes a Demon Heart, which provides the player an additional (sixth / seventh) accessory slot.
  - After the player has consumed a Demon Heart, additional ones will neither drop from Treasure Bags nor be consumable.
- The Merchant will begin selling the Drum Set and Drumstick if he was not already.
- The Angler will be able to ask for Angelfish and Cloudfish if he was not already.
Hardmode:
After defeating the Wall of Flesh for the first time, the status message “The ancient spirits of light and dark have been released.” displays and the world permanently converts to Hardmode. Hardmode brings new biomes, new and tougher enemies, and a vast array of new equipment.
Two diagonal stripes of Hallow and Corruption or Crimson form in a "V" pattern from the top of the world all the way to the bottom of the Underworld. Corruption/Crimson and Hallow will spread at a much faster rate, eventually covering vital areas such as the Jungle and any NPC housing if no action is taken.
Tips:
- If the Wall of Flesh is accidentally summoned, use of the Magic Mirror, despite killing the player, is usually inconsequential in practice, as the player is taken directly to their Spawn Point, meaning dropped money and, if playing on Mediumcore, dropped items can be recovered easily. Note that this does not work in Hardcore as hardcore characters only have 1 life.
- If the Wall of Flesh was recently summoned, make sure the Guide has respawned before attempting to summon the Wall of Flesh again to avoid the unnecessary loss of Voodoo Dolls.
- A common "arena" to fight the boss should consist of a long horizontal bridge spanning at least 1000 blocks.
  - The two main types of Wall of Flesh arenas are solid bridges and platform bridges, each with their own pros and cons.
    - Solid bridges are made out of solid blocks, blocking lasers from the bottom eye and allowing bouncing projectiles to rebound against it, but come at the cost of blocking most of the player's own projectiles and not allowing dropping down through to evade attacks.
    - Platform bridges allow projectiles to pass through them, allowing the user to damage all parts of the boss more often and drop down from them if needed to dodge lasers. However, it does not block the bottom eye's lasers, and certain projectiles like Beenades do not work well unless they hit solid blocks. In Expert Mode and higher, it is recommended to build these out of Stone Platforms, Ash Wood Platforms or Obsidian Platforms which will not be destroyed by dying Lava Slimes.
    - If the player does not want to build a bridge, acquiring the Lava Waders or their upgrades is necessary; they can also use the Water Walking Potion.
- Focus on The Hungry first before damaging the wall itself. The Hungry's damage and defense are boosted as the body takes damage, which will make them more difficult to kill if left for later.

Name: Queen Slime
Summoning: Queen Slime is summoned by using a Gelatin Crystal in The Hallow or Underground Hallow, at any time.
Aftermath: - If King Slime has already been defeated, the Princess will begin selling Royal Romance.
Tips:
- The Dart Pistol or Dart Rifle combined with Crystal Darts can make quick work of her minions as well as damage her multiple times per dart.
- Palladium armor can be useful due to the Rapid Healing buff it provides.
- Queen Slime herself has a relatively simple attack pattern. Half the threat comes from the minions she spawns, which can fill the screen with projectiles and quickly overwhelm the player. Killing or avoiding these should be a top priority.
- Stay in the air using wings or mounts during her first phase, as many of her attacks cannot reach the player there. During her second phase, the player should stay closer to the ground while occasionally luring her back up, as they can avoid many of her projectiles and minions due to their slow and predictable movement patterns.
- In Master Mode, The Black Spot mount allows the player to hover above all attacks in the first phase.
- Fight Queen Slime in daylight, since her attacks may be hard to see at night.
- Queen Slime can be killed easily before any other Hardmode bosses, and even before destroying Demon or Crimson Altars. The Crystal Assassin armor she drops will help the player survive in early Hardmode.
- Like most bosses, she is immune to lava, but her minions are not. An arena made of lava paired with Lava Waders or Terraspark Boots can make the fight significantly easier.
- Another effective strategy against her minions is to try to inflict multiple damaging debuffs at once. A good example of this is using the Shadowflame Knife paired with Frost armor and a Flask of Cursed Flames, as the three debuffs are often enough to finish off any of the slimes, even if only one knife hits.
- For magic users, the Life Drain is a very good choice for this fight. Because it deals continuous damage around the cursor, this allows the player to consistently damage the boss while focusing on dodging. Since the minions spawn from the center of the boss, it will deal some damage to them right as they spawn. In addition, the player gains a boost to their life regeneration while damaging an enemy.
- Use several disconnected platforms, which can allow her minions to fall down and away from the fight.
- Any wings paired with flight-boosting accessories and the Shield of Cthulhu (for its dash ability) makes dodging most of her attacks easy (but does not take care of her minions).
- The Daedalus Stormbow paired with Holy Arrows and summoned minions can take care of her minions.
- When fighting her in higher difficulties, never remain directly above multiple Crystal Slimes. Their spikes can kill the player in seconds.
- Invisibility Potions can be used to decrease spawn rates of other enemies and prevent the Heavenly Slimes from chasing after the player. Note that taking any damage will instantly cancel the buff, however.

Name: The Twins
Summoning:
Manual:
The Twins can be summoned manually using a Mechanical Eye at night (from 7:30 PM to 4:30 AM).
Random:
The Twins can also spawn naturally at the start of the night, as long as they have not yet been defeated at least once in the current world. Their arrival when spawning naturally is announced by the status message "This is going to be a terrible night...".
In order for the boss to spawn naturally, the following conditions must be fulfilled at dusk (7:30 PM):
- The world is in Hardmode and at least one Demon or Crimson Altar has been destroyed.
  - In worlds where the Skyblock special world seed is active and the tile threshold is not exceeded, The Twins can spawn even if no altars have been destroyed.
- No boss is already alive, and the Eye of Cthulhu is not already spawning naturally.
- None of the following events are active: Lantern Night, Old One's Army, Pumpkin Moon, or Frost Moon.
- Time is not being accelerated by the Enchanted Sundial or Enchanted Moondial.
If the conditions are met, there is a 1/10 (10%) chance for a random mechanical boss to spawn that has not yet been defeated in the world. This gives The Twins initially a spawn chance of 1/30 (3.33%) per night. If another mechanical boss is defeated first, the chance for The Twins to spawn increases to 1/20 (5%), and should both of the other mechanical bosses be defeated first, then The Twins have the full remaining 1/10 (10%) spawn chance per night.
Once The Twins have been selected to spawn, the status message appears and a hidden countdown of 1 minute 21 seconds begins. The Twins spawn at the end of the countdown, at 8:51 PM. Another check is performed at that time, with all of the following conditions needing to be fulfilled in order for the boss to spawn:
- At least one player is in the surface or Space layer.
  - Consequently, the natural spawning of The Twins can easily be prevented by being in a layer lower than the surface at 8:51 PM. Returning to the surface afterward will not cause The Twins to spawn either (unlike with the Eye of Cthulhu).
  - This restriction is lifted in worlds where the world spawn point is below the surface, such as worlds with the special world seed Remix active or the secret world seed Mole people. The Twins can spawn naturally in those worlds regardless of the player's position, whether they are above or below the surface.
- No boss is already alive.
- The Lunar Events are not active and the countdown for the spawning of the Moon Lord has not begun, either due to manual summoning or defeating the fourth Celestial Pillar.
- Time is not being accelerated by the Enchanted Sundial or Enchanted Moondial.
In singleplayer, exiting the world during the countdown also prevents The Twins from spawning naturally.
In worlds where the special seeds For the Worthy and The Constant are present but Celebration Mk 10 is not, The Twins will still be able to randomly spawn, even if they have been defeated before.
For the Worthy and Remix:
The Twins cannot be summoned in worlds where both the For the Worthy and Remix special world seeds are active, since the boss is part of Mechdusa instead.
Tips:
- Focus on defeating one eye completely first without inflicting too much damage on the other one. Battling The Twins while both are in their second form makes the battle much more difficult, especially in Expert Mode.
  - Spazmatism may be a better choice for defeating first, since its Cursed Flames are difficult to avoid without proper mobility equipment and buffs in its second phase. Retinazer is less deadly, as it cannot inflict debuffs and will not charge in its second phase, which helps the player attack it from a safe distance with ranged attacks.
  - In its first phase, Retinazer's accuracy is low enough that it will simply miss most shots against a stationary player. If Spazmatism is already defeated, even moderately tanky builds can maximize DPS for less effort by staying put, except to dodge charges.
- The Twins are only immune to Confused and Poisoned, so using a weapon that inflicts a debuff may be useful during the fight.
- A good arena for this boss is simply a long, flat plane. With Lightning Boots (or better) and a ranged or magic weapon, the player can continually outrun The Twins' attacks while firing back at them.
- In its second phase, Retinazer can only attack the player if it has an unobstructed line of sight. Hiding in a box prevents it from dealing any damage.
- A Gravitation Potion can be an excellent method of keeping distance from the Twins, allowing them to be attacked freely.

Name: Plantera
Summoning: After all three mechanical bosses have been defeated, Plantera's Bulbs will randomly spawn in the Underground Jungle (indicated by the status message "The jungle grows restless..."). These bulbs emit a faint pink light in dark areas and immediately summon Plantera nearby upon being destroyed, usually a fair distance off-screen.
ExpertMode:
In Expert Mode, there are a few significant differences in Plantera's attacks, aside from the default increased health and damage.
In the first form, her pink Seeds can travel through blocks, and all projectiles have limited homing capabilities. The cooldowns are also decreased:
In her second form, Plantera and Plantera's Tentacles move faster than normal. In addition, there are nine more Plantera's Tentacles, attached to Plantera's Hooks in groups of three. Furthermore, the eight tentacles that are attached to Plantera's body can respawn after they have been killed (this does not apply to the tentacles on the hooks). The rate is randomized, but it depends on the number of tentacles that are alive – if all tentacles are destroyed, a new tentacle spawns after 5 seconds, on average. This is increased by 5 seconds per living tentacle, hence it takes an average of 180 seconds for all eight tentacles to fully respawn. A single defeated tentacle will take 40 seconds to respawn, on average, assuming the other seven tentacles remain alive for the duration.
Aftermath:
Plantera always drops a Temple Key, which grants access to the Jungle Temple and the Golem boss.
A status message saying "Screams are echoing from the dungeon..." will appear upon Plantera's defeat, signaling that new, more difficult types of enemies will begin spawning in the Dungeon (see details). These enemies drop powerful new weapons, accessories, and other items. Dungeon Spirits will begin to appear when Dungeon enemies with more than 100 health are slain, which drop Ectoplasm, a new crafting material that offers access to the Pumpkin Moon and Frost Moon events, as well as Spectre Bars.
Additionally:
- The spread of the Corruption, Crimson, and Hallow is halved from their original speed.
- Biome Keys can now be used to open Biome Chests in the Dungeon.
- The Cyborg will be able to move in, thus allowing the Princess to arrive as well.
- The Truffle will begin selling the Autohammer, used to craft Shroomite Bars and upgrade rockets sold by the Cyborg.
- The Zoologist will begin selling the Mud Bud.
- The Dye Trader will begin rewarding the player with Pixie Dye, Wisp Dye, Infernal Wisp Dye, and Unicorn Wisp Dye in exchange for Strange Plants.
- The Witch Doctor will begin selling Leaf Wings, several items related to minion summoning, and Vials of Venom.
- The Demolitionist will begin selling Land Mines if the player has defeated a Pirate Invasion.
- Butchers, Psychos, Nailheads, Deadly Spheres, Dr. Man Flies, and Mothrons will start spawning during the Solar Eclipse event.
- The Prismatic Lacewing starts spawning in the aboveground Hallow, allowing the Empress of Light to be summoned.
- Hairstyles 146 & 163-165 are unlocked.
Tips:
- Excavate a sizable area to allow easier dodging before summoning Plantera. This can be done quicker with the use of Scarab Bombs.
  - Widening a Bee Hive in the Underground Jungle is a fast and effective way of making an arena for fighting Plantera (though care should be taken around the Larva).
  - Make sure the area has no background walls. This will significantly reduce Plantera's mobility in the second form as she does not have walls to hook onto.
  - Living Fire Blocks work excellently for lighting up the arena in place of torches; Plantera cannot grab onto them.
- Using a Gravitation Potion can help the player avoid damage from Thorn Balls laying on the ground, as the Thorn Balls obey gravity and fall to the floor. Alternatively, the player can use an arena that has a large empty area at the bottom for Thorn Balls to bounce in, well below the player and out of harm's way.
- Plantera's Bulbs can spawn in player-made Jungle biomes, which can provide a slightly easier way to fight Plantera.
- Narrow passages slow Plantera as it takes more time for her to grip the surrounding terrain.
- The use of a Hellevator combined with wings can make the Plantera fight drastically easier by spawning Plantera at a higher point in the Underground Jungle, and gliding downward while using a ranged or magic weapon.
- In Plantera's second form, her only ranged attack consists of the Spores which are very easy to kill. This means that keeping a distance is key to avoiding damage.
- An arena with Teleporters will make the player escape from Plantera's attacks easily.

Name: Golem
Summoning:
Golem is summoned by using a Lihzahrd Power Cell at the Lihzahrd Altar located in the final chamber of the Jungle Temple, at any time, and only if the current world is in Hardmode after Plantera is defeated. Upon pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Lihzahrd Altar, one Lihzahrd Power Cell is consumed from the player's inventory and Golem is summoned directly above the altar.
The Lihzahrd Altar can be relocated after being mined with a Picksaw or better. However, Golem will become enraged while outside of the Underground Jungle.
Aftermath:
- Cultists spawn at the Dungeon's entrance which, when killed, summon the Lunatic Cultist and then the Lunar Events (as long as certain other conditions are also met – see details).
  - For this to happen, Skeletron must have been defeated at least once, as the Old Man spawning will override the Cultists' spawning.
- Martian Probes begin spawning randomly, which can trigger the Martian Madness event.
- Summoning the Old One's Army after Golem has been defeated triggers the most difficult "Tier 3" version of the event, enabling the player to fight Betsy.
- Lihzahrd furniture can be decrafted via Shimmer.
- The Steampunker will begin to sell the Steampunk Wings, as well as the Lihzahrd Furnace (if she's in a Jungle).
- The Party Girl will begin to sell the Celebration.
Tips:
- In some cases, the terrain surrounding the Lihzahrd Altar will cause Golem to get stuck when it spawns. It can attack with its fists and projectiles but will be unable to jump around. Players can also recreate this condition by placing blocks near the altar.
- The three Lihzahrd Bricks under the Lihzahrd Altar cannot be actuated, hence it is impossible to relocate the altar prior to defeating Golem for the first time.

Name: Duke Fishron
Summoning:
Duke Fishron is summoned by fishing in the Ocean at any time, using a Truffle Worm as bait (see Notes for details). Once the bobber bobs, reeling in the line spawns Duke Fishron, who emerges from the water, pauses for a moment, and then begins attacking the player. Duke Fishron is invulnerable during his summoning animation.
Duke Fishron himself does not require any bosses to be defeated prior, meaning he can be summoned earlier than his intended stage of progression, and that Truffle Worms brought to a new world can be used to summon him.
Tips:
- The player should keep in mind their distance from the Ocean to prevent Duke Fishron from becoming enraged. One option is to build solid blocks around the Ocean boundaries to prevent accidentally enraging him.
- The Inferno Potion can come in handy during this fight to prevent taking any damage from Duke Fishron's Detonating Bubbles. While there is a slight delay between the damage intervals of the Inferno Potion's ring of fire, it is capable of clearing out groups of bubbles all at once.
  - Since Detonating Bubbles have a larger damaging area when they explode, the player should still keep some distance from them even when using the Inferno Potion.
- Players can build a platform along the top of the Ocean to avoid sinking. Water Walking Boots, their upgrades, or Water Walking Potions can be used as a substitute for platforms.
- Duke Fishron's charges aim for where the player is, not where they will be. Because of this, moving perpendicularly with his charges will cause him to completely miss. Dodging his charges can be as simple as moving in a zig-zag pattern or a triangle, or utilizing dashing equipment such as the Crystal Assassin armor, Shield of Cthulhu, Tabi, or Master Ninja Gear. The high mobility of the Winged Slime Mount can help as well.
- Should Duke Fishron and his Cthulunados be hard to see, the player can use Shine Potion and Hunter Potion. The Ichor debuff can also be inflicted on the boss to highlight him.
- Using an Anti-Gravity Hook on a block and continuously going in circles can successfully allow dodging every attack and dash from the boss when it is enraged.
- In Expert Mode, the Shield of Cthulhu can be used to great effect, providing brief invincibility frames when dashing into him.
  - The Chillet mount can be used to a similar effect since it too provides brief invulnerability.
- Due to Duke Fishron's fast speed in its third phase, it is suggested to use platforms in the arena to assist the player's movement.
- Though his difficulty makes him a post-Plantera or Golem boss, it is possible to defeat him before the mechanical bosses. Obtaining his weapons this early will make a significant portion of Hardmode (including the fights against the mechanical bosses) much easier to progress through.
- If fighting Duke Fishron after at least one mechanical boss has been defeated, and 500 max health has been obtained from Life Fruits, crafting Jungle Juice can give a slight edge, as it heals 30 more health than a Greater Healing Potion.

Name: The Torch God
Tips:
- Starting the event in an open area offers the player more room to dodge.
- Only proper Torches become part of the Torch God. Non-Torch light sources like lanterns can provide light to the area without becoming fireballs.
- Items that give the player a dodge chance, such as the Brain of Confusion, work against torch fireballs.
- Taken as an agility challenge, having mobility items like grappling hooks is preferred to help dodge the torch fireballs.
- Taken as an endurance challenge, having armor, buffs, and accessories that offer high defense is preferred to reduce the damage from the torch fireballs.
- The player can lessen enemy spawns using a Calming Potion and Peace Candle to reduce dangerous distractions from enemies, allowing the player to focus on dodging the fireballs.
  - Alternatively, the player can activate the event in a town for a greater spawn reduction. If the player fails, however, that town may become inaccessible until the player either completes the event or removes the Torches.
- Some Torches make their associated fireballs harder to see, while other Torches make it easier to see. The best, brightest Torch for dodging purposes is the White Torch, but is made from Diamonds and thus may be resource-intensive. The second best Torch is the Ultrabright Torch, and it is uncommonly sold from the Traveling Merchant. The third best Torch is the Ichor Torch. Depending on the environment, the Ice Torch, Hallowed Torch, and Jungle Torch might be the fourth best.
- The Torch God's Favor does not count as being in the inventory if it is in the trash slot, in a storage item like a Chest, or tossed to the ground. A player can use this to repeat the event.
Arena ideas:
These are some brief ideas for creating a favorable environment to take the event in:
- Create a large open area and line Torches around one edge to provide maximum dodging time.
- Build a small, square arena with the Torches clustered in the center. Lay down Ropes and walkways to be able to circle the Torches.
- Make a hellevator with a rope line and a Torch every 10 tiles, then place 101 Torches at the top and head down the rope line. By the time the player reaches the bottom, they should obtain Torch God's Favor.
- Lay down a loop of Minecart Tracks around a cluster of 101 Torches. Hammer the rails so that the Minecart rides in circles around the Torches, and make use of bumpers and rail intersections as necessary.

Name: Lunatic Cultist
Summoning: The Lunatic Cultist is summoned after killing the Cultists that spawn at the Dungeon's entrance after Skeletron and Golem have been defeated.
Aftermath:
Once the Lunatic Cultist is killed, the Lunar Events will be initiated with the message “Celestial creatures are invading!” Additionally, the Clothier will begin selling the Solar Cultist Clothes during the day and the Lunar Cultist Clothes at night.
Lunar Events:
Every time the Lunatic Cultist is defeated, the Lunar Events will begin. During this, four celestial pillars will spawn in the world, each themed around a damage class. Defeating all four pillars will summon the final boss.
Tips:
- The player should avoid defeating the Lunatic Cultist if they are not yet ready for the Lunar Events. Beating the Lunatic Cultist causes the Lunar Events to begin immediately, and there is no way to de-summon them thereafter (aside from defeating all of the Celestial Pillars).
- The real Lunatic Cultist can be distinguished from its decoys in a number of ways:
  - The real Cultist has pointed, angry eyes, while the decoys' eyes are round and neutral.
  - The real Cultist has a line on its hood while the decoys do not.
  - The real Cultist does not emit light, while the decoys do; however, this may only be apparent if fought at night.
  - When the ritual starts, the real Cultist is the copy that is furthest away from the player.
  - When hovered over, decoys will always display as having 10000/10000 health, while the real Cultist will display its true health value instead.
- Using Autopause grants as much time as needed for identifying the real Cultist.
- Attacking a decoy Cultist is not a bad idea if the player uses the Vampire Knives. The resulting Phantasm Dragon is very long and may be easily targeted to restore some life.
- Many of the Lunatic Cultist's attacks can be blocked by hiding behind solid blocks, including its lightning bolts and fireballs. A weapon that attacks through blocks or a yoyo can be used to deal damage.
- There is little reason to farm the Lunatic Cultist itself, as its only non-vanity drops are Greater Healing Potions and the Ancient Manipulator, the latter only needing to be obtained once. However, defeating it is the only way to access the Lunar Events and Lunar Fragments.
- If the lock on mechanic selects the Lunatic Cultist as the target, the target is dispelled every time it teleports.
- Depending on the world size and generation, one of the Celestial Pillars will often spawn immediately within the vicinity of the player upon defeating the Lunatic Cultist. If this happens when the player is unprepared, and the background changes to indicate a Celestial Pillar has spawned near the player, it is recommended to immediately pick up the Lunatic Cultist's drops and teleport back to a safe base using a Magic Mirror or Recall Potion to prevent from being unexpectedly ambushed by dangerous enemies spawned from the Lunar Events.

Name: Moon Lord
Summoning: The Moon Lord will spawn after destroying the four Celestial Pillars or can be summoned manually using a Celestial Sigil in any world where Golem has been defeated. The status message “Impending doom approaches...” indicates the Moon Lord's spawning countdown. During the countdown, the screen will go dim and all objects, tiles, and walls will oscillate back and forth, and then go back to normal, and the sound volume will gradually decrease, eventually becoming completely silent. If the Moon Lord is spawned by destroying the Celestial Pillars, it takes 60 seconds for him to spawn, and the screen effect will appear 5 times; each time the screen will go darker and all objects and walls will oscillate more violently. If using a Celestial Sigil to summon the Moon Lord, it takes 12 seconds for him to spawn, and the screen effect will only appear once.
Aftermath:
After defeating the Moon Lord, the credits will appear while the song Journey's End plays. Besides his other loot, the Moon Lord always drops Luminite, allowing the player to craft endgame armor sets, tools, furniture, and accessories.
Additionally:
- The Princess will begin selling Music Box (Journey's End).
- The Steampunker will begin selling Yellow Solution, White Solution, and Brown Solution used for the Clentaminator.
- The Dye Trader will begin rewarding the player with Skiphs' Blood in exchange for Strange Plants.
- The Cyborg will sell the Portal Gun Station, so long as the player has the Portal Gun from the Moon Lord in their inventory.
- The Traveling Merchant now has the chance to sell the Not a Kid, nor a Squid and Moonman & Company paintings.
- The Rod of Harmony, Terraformer, and Bottomless Shimmer Bucket become available via Shimmer transmutation.
- Hairstyle 134 is unlocked if the Martian Madness has been defeated already.
- The world icon gains a special border in the world selection menu.
Tips:
- Keeping a distance while dodging the Moon Lord's attacks is crucial. In particular, his Phantasmal Deathray should be avoided at all costs.
  - Useful items that increase the player's mobility include Gravitation Potions, fast wings like the Fishron, Betsy's, or Empress Wings, the Rod of Discord, items allowing to dash (e.g. the Tabi or its upgrade, the Master Ninja Gear), the Soaring Insignia, and numerous mount-summoning items like the Gelatinous Pillion, Shrimpy Truffle, Cosmic Car Key, or Witch's Broom. The player might also consider constructing a skybridge made out of Asphalt Blocks or Minecart Tracks (with a minecart boosted by the Minecart Upgrade Kit).
    - Items that provide high horizontal speed (Minecart Upgrade Kit-boosted minecarts, Soaring Insignia with hoverable wings, Hexxed Branch, etc.) allow the player to outrange the Phantasmal Deathray from the True Eyes of Cthulhu.
  - Using homing weapons or ammo like Chlorophyte Bullets allow the player to focus on dodging.
  - It is possible to avoid the deathray by staying close to the Moon Lord's head, and moving up and around the central eye as it fires the ray. The ray does not sweep as quickly when near its origin point, due to the nature of rotational movement, so being as close to its origin as possible makes it easier to maneuver around.
- Teleporting away from the Moon Lord to get healing from the Nurse might result in her death, due to the Moon Lord immediately teleporting to the player.
  - In multiplayer, the Moon Lord will attack the nearest player. Players can take turns teleporting home to get healing from the Nurse.
- The Moon Lord is vulnerable to almost all debuffs, most notably Ichor and Betsy's Curse, which can dramatically speed up the fight. However, since the Moon Lord's eyes remove all debuffs when they close, the player will have to reapply them accordingly.
- It is advisable to kill the eye on the head first. It is the only eye capable of firing the Phantasmal Deathray and remains closed for significantly longer than the eyes in the hands. If the player waits to kill the head last, they may have to deal with two True Eyes of Cthulhu for a longer amount of time.
- While the frequently-applied Moon Bite debuff disables the healing effects of Vampire Knives and the Spectre Hood, it does not disable health regeneration boosts, hence the effects of the Nebula armor and the Life Drain are not affected.
- Some of the Moon Lord's attacks can be avoided using the 200 NPC spawn limit, and the True Eyes of Cthulhu can be prevented from spawning completely if the limit is reached.
- Due to the Moon Lord's attacks bypassing invincibility frames, special setups are recommended to bypass his attacks.
- Moon Leech Clots will always reach the Moon Lord's mouth in the same amount of time. They travel toward it at a variable rate, remaining completely stationary (or at least apparently so) if the Moon Lord is in his default position behind the player. As a result of this, though it may seem counterintuitive, it is actually beneficial to be closer to the mouth to destroy Moon Leech Clots, as they will not move away as quickly.
- While the Phantasmal Spheres the Moon Lord shoots can pierce all NPCs, the Phantasmal Bolts get destroyed upon contact with an NPC, potentially being a viable option for players trying to avoid the bolts.
- For those farming the Moon Lord for the Meowmere and Star Wrath in order to craft the Zenith: For each kill, there is a 58.33% chance of obtaining neither, a 38.88% chance of obtaining one, and a 2.77% chance of obtaining both.

Name: Martian Saucer
Tips:
- To dodge the Martian Saucer's laser machineguns, hover above or below its lasers. To dodge its missiles, run away from it as it shoots so that most of the missiles hit the ground in front of the player.
- To avoid getting caught in its deathray, a recommended strategy is to position oneself above the Martian Saucer, either by flying above it with wings or by teleporting with the Rod of Discord or Hook of Dissonance. During the second phase, move as far away from the Martian Saucer as possible during its brief phase transition, and, when the Martian Saucer is firing deathrays, the player should move in the same direction as it if they cannot get above it, which can be supplemented by equipment that provides dashing such as the Tabi and its upgrades. With well-timed dashes, the deathray can be completely avoided.
- When the Cute Fishron's "wet" bonus is activated, the player can fly slightly faster than the Martian Saucer.

Name: Empress of Light
Summoning:
The Empress of Light is summoned by killing a Prismatic Lacewing, at any time.
Prismatic Lacewings spawn in The Hallow on the Surface between dusk (7:30 PM) and midnight (12:00 AM) once Plantera has been defeated. They can be caught with a Bug Net (or its upgrades), then released elsewhere and killed by the player. If released outside of the Hallow, a Prismatic Lacewing will disappear almost immediately.
The Empress of Light herself does not require any bosses to be defeated prior, meaning she can be summoned earlier than her intended stage of progression, and that Prismatic Lacewings brought to a new world can be used to summon her.
Tips:
- The Guide to Critter Companionship can be used to avoid accidentally summoning the boss, as it prevents the player from damaging critters, including the Prismatic Lacewing.
- Capturing Prismatic Lacewings with a Bug Net rather than killing them immediately allows the player to fight the Empress of Light at a proper time and place once prepared.
- Although the Prismatic Lacewing can only spawn at night, the Empress of Light can be spawned at any time of day using captured Prismatic Lacewings.
- If the Prismatic Lacewing is released outside of the Hallow, it will disappear very quickly. To ensure that it gets killed, the player can place the critter directly into a stationary area-of-effect projectile, such as a Clinger Staff's flame pillar or a Rainbow Gun's rainbow.
- A Rod of Discord will help the player evade some of the Empress of Light's attacks.
- If attempting to fight the Empress of Light during the day to obtain the Terraprisma, defense and damage resistance should be completely disregarded in favor of damage and mobility, as any damage taken will be beyond lethal regardless.
  - The dash ability from the Shield of Cthulhu, Master Ninja Gear, or Solar Flare armor can increase mobility.
  - Wings with hover or fast acceleration capabilities, such as Fishron or Betsy's Wings or the Jetpack, can be quite effective for dodging.
  - Dodges from Holy Protection, the Black Belt and its upgrades, and the Brain of Confusion will not protect the player from death, so it is recommended to replace them with armor and accessories that increase damage output.
  - If using the Rod of Discord during her daytime fight, the Chaos State debuff can be disregarded entirely unless the damage from it would also kill the player. Losing a fraction of health to Chaos State is far better than losing all of it to one of the Empress of Light's attacks.
  - A riskier strategy would see the use of flying mounts instead of wings or boots, which would free up accessory slots for increased damage output.
  - Arenas do not require structures that boost defense or health regeneration, like Campfires, Heart Lanterns, or Bast Statues, as taking any damage instantly kills the player.
- Use weapons that are capable of dealing damage reliably from long range or have homing, such as the Blizzard Staff, Possessed Hatchet, Scourge of the Corruptor, Tsunami, Aerial Bane, Snowman Cannon, Chain Gun, or Tactical Shotgun with Chlorophyte Bullets.
- A large arena constructed of Asphalt Blocks and layers of platforms is highly recommended, especially with the demand for mobility while fighting the Empress of Light during the day.
- She is not immune to any practical debuffs. This can be a good extra source of damage, especially with the use of Ichor, Betsy's Curse, or Daybroken.
- It is best to stay at an average level or below the Empress of Light as she zips above the player's position after every attack she does, making it more likely for the player to be killed by contact damage during the day or take unnecessary hits during the night.

Name: Betsy
Tips:
- The On Fire! debuff is a major source of damage. Note that it negates life regen from Nebula armor's set bonus – hence, if the player is unable to avoid Betsy's flame breath attack, it might make the armor ineffective.
  - The Obsidian Skin Potion can prevent the debuff.
  - A floating pool of water (utilizing Bubbles) can be used to cancel the On Fire! debuff. Honey will also cancel the debuff and also give extra life regeneration, but slows down the player's movement while submerged in it unless they are using Flipper Potions.
  - This does not apply to life-stealing effects such as the Spectre armor Hood set bonus or the Vampire Knives. It does not affect the Life Drain's health regen boost either.

Name: Ogre
Tips:
- Although the Ogre has a powerful close-ranged club swing attack, he can be easily maneuvered around due to his generally slow speed, making it easy for the player to keep their distance and dodge his snot ball and melee attacks.
- Using yoyos with the Yoyo Bag equipped can be an extremely effective method of killing the Ogre.
- In Tier 3, the club swing attack deals 472 damage in Master Mode, which can kill players in one hit. This is easily the most damage that can be dealt by a single attack from any of the enemies in the Old One's Army event, even surpassing all of Betsy's attacks.
- An easy method to dodge the Ogre's stomp is to either jump before he lands or to constantly stay in the air by using wings, accessories that provide extra jumps, or by using flying mounts, such as those from The Black Spot, Witch's Broom, Shrimpy Truffle, or Cosmic Car Key.
  - Another easy way to dodge his jump attack is to fight the Old One's Army in space, where the very low gravity prolongs his jump to extreme lengths. This makes it easy to walk away before he lands.
  - It is not very wise to use a platform above the ground when fighting the Ogre for he may leap onto said platform when performing his leap. Despite the particles of the slam coming from the ground, the Ogre's slam hitbox is still carried with him to greater heights.
- The Oozed debuff does not affect the speed of flying mounts that are not in contact with the ground, making them quite useful while fighting Ogres.
- It is recommended to kill the Ogre before he is halfway between the Mysterious Portal and the Eternia Crystal because he will then begin to target the Crystal. His snot balls can also hit the player at this stage.

Name: Mourning Wood
Tips:
- Pay attention to when a Mourning Wood stops walking, as it is about to perform one of its two ranged attacks.
- It is advisable not to enter a small room while fighting a Mourning Wood because its "Flaming Wood" attack can go through walls.
- The Mourning Wood's "Greek Fire" attacks cannot pass through water, therefore submerging the mini-boss at least halfway up is an easier way to defeat it. Note the "Flaming Wood" attacks do pass through water.
- The Mourning Wood can be defeated with relative ease by aiming the North Pole above it so it gets hit by several of its snowflake projectiles.

Name: Pumpking
Tips:
- The Flairon can be very effective against the Pumpking, who tends to float right above players (well within the range of the Flairon and its homing bubbles), causing very high damage per hit.
- The Pumpking's contact damage is relatively lower than the damage inflicted by his projectiles, especially his Flaming Scythes. Using wings and other flight-based accessories like the Soaring Insignia to fly closer towards his head while tanking his contact damage with high defense may help the player avoid taking excessive amounts of damage, especially in cases when they are being attacked by multiple Pumpkings at once.
- High-mobility items, such as the Anti-Gravity Hook, the Tabi and its upgrades, or the Shield of Cthulhu, allow for easier handling of the Pumpking.

Name: Everscream
Tips:
- Most of the Everscream's attacks can easily be avoided by staying on platforms high enough above the ground, as the attacks have limited range. Attacking with any ranged or long-range melee weapon from there trivializes the fight.
- The Everscream is one of the few mini-bosses whose attacks can be shielded, as its Ornament and Pine Needle attacks do not go through blocks.
- Unlike Mourning Wood, the Everscream's attacks do not deal increased damage after its health drops past 25%.

Name: Santa-NK1
Tips:
- Players should note that its Present launcher and Missile barrage attacks are highly inaccurate.
- Using wings to fly over it back and forth will make its chain gun and the Missile barrage harder to hit the player.
- The Razorpine and Golden Shower/Betsy's Wrath are very effective against it. Hitting it first with the Golden Shower/Betsy's Wrath lowers its defense, increasing the DPS of the Razorpine. This is highly effective with Spectre armor with the Spectre Hood as it fully heals the player no matter how low the player's health is.

Name: Ice Queen
Tips:
- Both of the Ice Queen's attacks will inflict the Chilled debuff, which slows the player's movement speed, and Frost Waves will sometimes inflict the Frozen debuff which completely immobilizes the player. Equipping a Hand Warmer or Ankh Shield will negate these effects and potentially make the fight much less frustrating.
- Drinking a Warmth Potion is recommended as it will significantly lower the damage the Ice Queen can inflict on the player, and it will last for the entire duration of the event.
- The Frozen debuff causes players to exit their mounts. This may kill a player without immunity to fall damage if inflicted at a high enough point in the sky.
- The Ice Queen is most vulnerable while executing her twirl attack, when she spins in place rapidly and shoots Frost Shards in all directions. This is the only time she stays in one spot.
- The distribution of the Ice Queen's Frost Shards during her twirl attack is weighted such that the projectiles have a significantly higher chance of shooting near-diagonally than near-vertically or near-horizontally. Thus, players standing roughly along one cardinal direction from the Ice Queen (up, down, left, or right from her) have a lesser chance of being hit than players standing diagonally from her.
- To mitigate her damage, using wings and possibly movement-enhancing accessories for chasing and dodging, in addition to equipping a Cross Necklace/Star Veil combined with lifesteal (Spectre armor or Vampire Knives), proves very effective.
- When attacking with frost waves, she will not fire any towards the player if they are above her. This can be easily be achieved with mounts that have infinite flight time such as the Witch's Broom, and wings using the Soaring Insignia.

Name: Flying Dutchman
Tips:
- Any weapons that can hit multiple targets at once are good for taking out the cannons.
- Due to the way it moves and the way the cannonballs fire, it is very easy to find positions where it cannot hit the player, yet they can hit it.
  - Weapons that can be used in these situations include any kind of summoning weapon, the Daedalus Stormbow, the Meteor Staff, the Nimbus Rod, and the Flying Knife.
- Due to the fact that they stop upon hitting a wall, and continuously spawn pirates, the Flying Dutchmen can be stopped above a half-block deep pit of lava (or other trap) and used to farm the various items pertaining to the Pirate Invasion.
- Farming for the Lucky Coin, Discount Card, or Gold Ring is most efficient from killing the Flying Dutchman, rather than from common pirates. After getting event progress to 50%, one can ensure 10 Flying Dutchmen per event by getting high enough above the ground (using a small platform or flying mount), but not too high, so that spawned enemies will be in the "Active Rectangle" and will despawn after 12.5 seconds, and then spawn again. Using this method, only Flying Dutchmen and Parrots can reach the player. Parrots can be killed safely as they do not count towards event progress.
- A Minecart with a sufficiently long track is useful for dodging the Flying Dutchman's attacks, and can then be attacked with ranged or magic weapons from the Minecart.
